Hi Samuel —

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. To produce a concrete Dedicated proposal and a tokens/sec runway model I need a couple of quick datapoints from your engineering/prod team: 

- Peak concurrent active sessions (web + API) during your busiest 30-minute window
- Average tokens per request (prompt + expected response) and a 95th percentile tokens figure if you have it
- Target p95 latency SLO for interactive calls (ms) and for batch jobs (if any)
- Expected steady-state QPS and a burst multiplier (e.g., 3x for product launches)

If you can attach the traffic export (CSV) or just paste a short profile I can run a preliminary slab/safety buffer calc and share an initial sizing today.

We typically model two scenarios: conservative (30% safety buffer + canary fallback to quantized variant) and aggressive (15% buffer, rely on autoscaling bursts). I want to make sure the numbers fit your SLA and budget.

Cheers,
Priya

Samuel —

Got the CSV, thanks — useful breakdown. I ran a quick back-of-envelope using your 30-minute peak (1,200 sessions) and tokens stats:

Assumptions used:
- Average tokens per request = 420
- p95 tokens = 1,100
- Concurrency conversion: assume 60% of sessions active across the 30m window -> ~720 active requests spread over 30 minutes -> ~0.4 req/sec steady within that window, but bursts are concentrated so we model peak QPS from your 36 req/sec observed multiplier

Prelim results (very conservative):
- Tokens/sec at peak burst (36 req/sec * 1,100 tokens) = 39,600 tokens/sec
- Tokens/sec at steady peak (9 req/sec * 420 tokens) = 3,780 tokens/sec

Sizing note: single A100-like GPU serving a quantized 8B model at low-latency can sustained ~12–18k tokens/sec depending on sequence length and batching. A 13B at similar latency typically lands at ~6–9k tokens/sec.

Initial Dedicated slab suggestion:
- If you want p95 <= 250ms on the 13B variant across the burst window, we'd recommend ~6 GPUs (13B-optimized) with continuous batching and KV cache warm to cover ~39.6k tokens/sec (6 * 6.5k = 39k tokens/sec — borderline). Add a 20% safety buffer -> 7–8 GPUs.
- If you choose the 8B quantized variant (with small quality delta), 3–4 GPUs would cover the burst with a 30% buffer (3 * 15k = 45k tokens/sec).

I'll convert this into a formal slab calc and include latency model curves (p50/p95) for both options. Two clarifying Qs before I finalize:
1) How tolerant are you to a small fraction (~5–10%) of requests falling back to a quantized variant during hard bursts?
2) Any regional routing constraints? Are all sessions US-only or global?

I'll loop in Karthik and Ben for pricing and commitment structure once you confirm tolerances.

Thanks —
Priya
Priya Natarajan
Senior Account Lead, Redwood Inference

From: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.ai>

Date: Tue, 12 Jul 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Internal: Elysia sizing — calc and recommendation (draft)

Team —

Summary of what Samuel sent (see CSV). Peak burst tokens/sec = ~39.6k. They want p95 interactive <= 250ms; >800 token flows can be higher. My initial modeling yields two paths:

Option A — Quality-first (13B model):
- Baseline per-GPU tokens/sec: 6.5k (p50 latency ~120ms, p95 ~230ms with steady KV cache and batching)
- GPUs required (no buffer): math = ceil(39,600 / 6,500) = 7 GPUs -> but p95 margin is tight; recommend 8 GPUs to get ~20% headroom and account for cold cache/OS jitter
- Operational notes: prefer pinned cache warmers, reserved KV cache lanes, and canary rollout for major model updates

Option B — Cost-first (8B quantized):
- Baseline per-GPU tokens/sec: 15k (p50 ~90ms, p95 ~200–220ms)
- GPUs required (no buffer): ceil(39,600 / 15,000) = 3 GPUs; recommend 4 GPUs with 30% buffer -> covers burst and gives runway for growth

Recommendation (sales-balanced): propose a phased commitment — start with 4 GPUs dedicated quantized (8B) + 2 on-demand 13B instances for higher-quality traffic. Convert to 8 dedicated GPUs (13B) on a 12-month committed tier if they opt for higher quality after the trial.

Pricing considerations: we can present a blended committed price for the 12-month plan with a canary rollback SLA and 30% ingress buffer. Ben can you draft a price sheet for 4 quantized dedicated GPUs + 2 on-demand 13B for a 90-day pilot then a 12-month convert?

Also: ask product to pre-warm KV cache for the pilot. Grace — can you prepare the rollout checklist (canary endpoints, fallback to hosted API, telemetry hooks)?

Thanks,
Priya

Priya — good modeling. A couple of product/contract levers to mention to customer that help reduce the committed footprint:

1) Autoscaling burst credit: offer a 90-day pilot with committed baseline (4 GPUs) plus a pooled burst credit of 2 additional GPUs that they pay for usage-wise if they exceed baseline. This reduces commit risk for them.
2) Quantized fallback policy: route up to 15% of traffic to the 8B quantized variant automatically when queue depth grows; preserves quality for the bulk while limiting worst-case latency.
3) Pre-warm KV cache windows: for predictable promotions we can schedule a 60-minute pre-warm job to reduce cold-cache p95 impact.

Commercially, propose:
- Pilot: 4x A100-equivalent dedicated (8B quantized) + 2x on-demand 13B (paid at usage rates). Pilot price = blended monthly pilot fee + overage at usage.
- Conversion: Option to convert to 8x dedicated 13B GPUs at a 12-month committed rate with a 15% discount for 12-month prepay.

Ben — can you produce two quotes (pilot and convert) and include a DocuSign link and a commitment SLA (we include a 99.5% uptime target for the Dedicated slab).

Thanks,
Karthik

Subject: Redwood proposal: pilot sizing & recommended Dedicated runway (ELY-2027-03)

Samuel —

Appended below is our recommended pilot + conversion path based on the traffic you shared. If this looks reasonable we can issue the DocuSign and schedule a two-week kickoff to pre-warm caches and verify telemetry.

Pilot (90 days) — recommended:
- 4x Dedicated A100-equivalent GPUs running quantized 8B variant (covers ~45k tokens/sec with 30% buffer)
- 2x On-demand 13B instances (warm standby, billed by usage)
- Autoscaling burst pool: charged as metered usage when the pooled baseline is exceeded (we include first 1,000 GPU-hours at no charge for first month)
- SLA: 99.5% uptime on dedicated slab, canary rollback and fallback to hosted API in case of major regressions

P95 runway math (pilot):
- Pilot baseline tokens/sec capacity: 4 * 15,000 = 60k tokens/sec -> covers the 39.6k observed burst with ~50% headroom
- Expected p95 (8B quantized): ~200–220ms for common sequences; for >800 token generations expect up to 400–500ms during the highest peaks without additional on-demand 13B capacity

Conversion option (12-month committed):
- 8x Dedicated A100-equivalent GPUs running 13B optimized variant
- Expected tokens/sec: 8 * 6.5k = 52k tokens/sec; with model/kernel tuning we target p95 <= 250ms across most traffic and will include a 10% performance buffer

Attachments: Redwood-proposal-ELY-2027.pdf (proposal + pricing), initial_slab_calc.xlsx (detailed calc), Elysia_traffic_profile.csv (your upload). DocuSign link: https://docusign.example.com/ELY-2027

Next steps:
1) If pilot looks good, sign DocuSign and we'll schedule kickoff for pre-warm + canary rollout (target start: two weeks after sign).
2) We will provision the 4 dedicated quantized GPUs in a US region (recommended near their primary user base) and configure autoscaling pool.

Happy to jump on a 30-min wrap-up call — Karthik and Ben are available early next week.

Thanks,
Priya
